title: Real batteries: resistance, rate and energy density

concepts.label: open-circuit voltage
concepts.definition: The voltage between a cell's terminals when no current flows; it equals what the chemistry predicts (E° corrected by Nernst) and depends on the state of charge.

concepts.label: voltage under load (sag)
concepts.definition: The terminal voltage while current flows, always below the open-circuit voltage on discharge; the gap (sag) grows with the current and disappears when the load is removed.

concepts.label: resistance (ohm)
concepts.definition: The volts of push needed per ampere of current through something: 1 Ω = 1 V/A; a device of resistance R on a cell draws I = E / (R + r).

concepts.label: internal resistance, V = E − I·r
concepts.definition: The lumped resistance r of everything the current crosses inside a cell (electrolyte, separator, electrode particles, foils), so that terminal voltage V = E − I·r on discharge and E + I·r on charge.

concepts.label: resistive heat I²r
concepts.definition: The volts lost inside a cell become heat at a rate of I²·r watts; the device gets V·I, the maximum deliverable power is E²/4r at V = E/2, and a short circuit turns everything into heat.

concepts.label: overpotential
concepts.definition: The difference between an electrode's (or cell's) voltage while current flows and its equilibrium value: ohmic loss plus activation (tilting the reaction off equilibrium) plus ion-transport (concentration) loss; internal resistance is its straight-line approximation.

concepts.label: C-rate
concepts.definition: Current divided by rated capacity: 1C empties the rated capacity in one hour, 2C in half an hour, 0.2C in five hours.

concepts.label: usable capacity vs rate (cut-off voltage)
concepts.definition: Discharge stops at a cut-off voltage; at higher currents the lower terminal voltage reaches it earlier, so the capacity and (even more) the energy actually delivered shrink as the rate rises.

concepts.label: specific power (W/kg)
concepts.definition: Power a cell can deliver per kilogram of its mass; the counterpart of specific energy (Wh/kg).

concepts.label: power vs energy (Ragone plot)
concepts.definition: A log–log plot of specific energy against specific power, one point per complete discharge at one rate; each curve is flat and then falls off a cliff, and diagonals are lines of equal runtime (energy ÷ power).

concepts.label: theoretical vs practical specific energy
concepts.definition: Theoretical Wh/kg counts only the reactants of the cell reaction; practical Wh/kg divides by the mass of the whole cell (electrolyte, current collectors, separator, case) and is typically 20–60% of the theoretical value.

concepts.label: volumetric energy density (Wh/L)
concepts.definition: Energy stored per litre of cell volume; the figure that matters when space rather than weight is the limit.

concepts.label: series vs parallel
concepts.definition: Cells in series (plus to minus in a chain) add their voltages at one cell's capacity; cells in parallel (like terminals joined) add their capacities at one cell's voltage and share the current.

concepts.label: battery pack (s × p)
concepts.definition: Cells wired s groups in series, each of p cells in parallel ('4s2p'): voltage s × V, capacity p × Q, energy = number of cells × energy per cell, pack resistance s × r / p.

concepts.label: coulombic efficiency
concepts.definition: Charge delivered on discharge divided by charge put in on charge (Ah out ÷ Ah in); below 100% because some charging current drives side reactions such as gassing or SEI growth.

concepts.label: energy efficiency
concepts.definition: Energy delivered divided by energy put in over a full cycle (Wh out ÷ Wh in) = coulombic efficiency × average discharge voltage ÷ average charge voltage; always lower than the coulombic efficiency.

constant-voltage taper at the end of Li-ion charging (one-line caveat)

summary: Running example: one 18650 Li-ion cell (typical rounded figures: 3.60 V resting, 3.0 Ah, 46 g, 16.5 mL, internal resistance 0.05 Ω, cut-off 2.5 V), followed from a voltmeter reading that sags under load (0.05 V per ampere) through V = E − I·r, I²r heat (max power at 36 A, 72 A short circuit), the three overpotentials, C-rate discharge curves, a Ragone plot against lead–acid, NiMH and LFP cells, theoretical vs practical Wh/kg and Wh/L (lead–acid 171 → 38, NiMH ≈ 215 → 89, Li-ion ≈ 380 → 235 Wh/kg), s × p packs, and coulombic vs energy efficiency. The capstone is a pack designer (chemistry, s, p, constant-power load → runtime, sag, heat, usable capacity) with an e-bike mission (36 V, 250 W for 2 h, ≤ 3 kg; solved by 10s5p Li-ion). Hooks for later lessons: 'open-circuit voltage minus overpotentials', activation/ohmic/transport losses (reused by the fuel-cell polarisation curve), the Ragone plot with runtime diagonals, 'practical is 20–60% of theoretical', energy efficiency = coulombic × voltage ratio (round-trip efficiency), and energy and power being fixed together in a cell (flow batteries separate them).
